statement: The Fisher information $\mathcal{I}(\theta)$ is defined as the variance of the score, or equivalently the expected value of the observed information: $\mathcal{I}(\theta) = \operatorname{E}\left[\left.\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\log f(X;\theta)\right)^{2}\,\,\right|\,\,\theta\right] = \int_{\mathbb{R}}\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\log f(x;\theta)\right)^{2}f(x;\theta)\,dx$. If $\theta$ is a vector, the regularity conditions hold for every component of $\theta$, and the Fisher information matrix is used to calculate covariance matrices associated with maximum-likelihood estimates.

symbols.meaning: Fisher information (or Fisher information matrix for a parameter vector)
unknown parameter of the distribution modeling X
observable random variable (single sample or collection of samples)
probability density function modeling X given parameter \theta
score function (partial derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to \theta)

properties.why: It is defined as the variance of the score, or the expectation of a squared quantity

properties.property: Zero expectation of the score: $\operatorname{E}\left[\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\log f(X;\theta)\,\,\right|\,\,\theta\right] = 0$
properties.why: Differentiating under the integral sign yields $\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x;\theta)\,dx = \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}(1) = 0$
Represents the curvature of the support curve (graph of the log-likelihood) under regularity conditions when $\log f(x;\theta)$ is twice differentiable

properties.property: Log-likelihood substitution: log-likelihood $l(\theta; X)$ can be substituted for $\log f(X; \theta)$ in the definition
properties.why: Likelihood is proportional to $f(X;\theta)$, so their logarithms differ by a constant independent of $\theta$ and have identical derivatives

properties.property: Additivity across independent samples: for $n$ independent distributions $\mathcal{I}(\theta) = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathcal{I}_i(\theta)$, and for $n$ i.i.d. samples $\mathcal{I}(\theta) = n \mathcal{I}_1(\theta)$
properties.why: Fisher information is additive over statistically independent observations

properties.property: Cramér–Rao bound: $\operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}) \geq \frac{1}{\mathcal{I}(\theta)}$ for any unbiased estimator $\hat{\theta}(X)$
properties.why: Follows from the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality applied to the estimator error and the score function

assumptions.assumption: The partial derivative of $f(X; \theta)$ with respect to $\theta$ exists almost everywhere on a set not depending on $\theta$
assumptions.breaks_when: The density fails to be differentiable with respect to $\theta$ on sets independent of $\theta$

assumptions.assumption: The integral of $f(X; \theta)$ can be differentiated under the integral sign with respect to $\theta$
assumptions.breaks_when: Conditions permitting the interchange of integration and differentiation fail, invalidating the zero-mean score identity

assumptions.assumption: The support of $f(X; \theta)$ does not depend on $\theta$
assumptions.breaks_when: The support boundary varies with $\theta$, such as for a $\operatorname{Uniform}(0, \theta)$ distribution

assumptions.assumption: For vector $\theta$, regularity conditions hold for every component of $\theta$
assumptions.breaks_when: Regularity conditions fail for any individual component of $\theta$

failure_modes.signature: Fisher information computed from the definition fails to satisfy standard properties such as the Cramér–Rao bound or standard asymptotic properties
failure_modes.cause: Density has parameter-dependent support boundaries (e.g., Uniform(0, θ)), violating regularity conditions 1 and 3

failure_modes.mode: Invalid differentiation under the integral sign
failure_modes.signature: Expected score is non-zero, or the negative expected second derivative does not equal the variance of the score
failure_modes.cause: Density violates regularity conditions permitting the exchange of differentiation with respect to θ and integration over X
